literal: The pretended worth of an unlearned person, when meeting others and speaking, ruin will occur to it.
translation: The apparent dignity of an unlearned person will instantly collapse the moment they meet others and begin to speak.
modern: கல்லாத ஒருவனுடைய தகைமையானது (மதிப்பு), அவன் பிறரைச் சந்தித்துப் பேசத் தொடங்கும்போது கெட்டுப் போய்விடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights how silence can mask ignorance, but only temporarily. An unlearned person might carry themselves with an air of dignity and worth ('தகைமை') that deceives others at first glance. However, the moment they come face-to-face ('தலைப்பெய்து') with others and engage in intellectual discourse ('சொல்லாட'), their lack of knowledge is exposed. Their superficial reputation immediately suffers a ruinous collapse ('சோர்வு படும்') because speech inevitably reveals the depth of one's mind.
